conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode; EMA(close, n)[k] is the n-bar exponential average k bars ago; highest(x, n)[k] / lowest(x, n)[k] are windows of n bars ending k bars ago; avgRange(n) = average(high - low, n); tickSize is the instrument's minimum move

candidates.name: BullTrendBar
candidates.quote: Trends can be very steep, with a series of trend bars with large bodies, very little overlap between adjacent bars, and small tails.
candidates.description: Shared primitive for this chapter: the current bar is a bull trend bar, closing up with a body that is at least a fraction of its range.

complexity.reason: single-bar arithmetic on open/high/low/close

notes: Brooks gives no number; 0.6 reads 'large body'. Other chapters define the same primitive; merge in dedup.

candidates.name: SwingPivot
candidates.quote: In a bull trend, the swings should be trending upward, meaning that each pullback should be above the prior pullback and result in a new high.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a swing low is a bar whose low is below the lows of the pivotStrength bars on each side; a swing high is the mirror. Provides lastSwingLow / priorSwingLow / lastSwingHigh / priorSwingHigh for the swing-structure candidates below. Confirmed only pivotStrength bars after the pivot bar.
candidates.pseudocode: isSwingLow(k) = low[k] < lowest(low, pivotStrength)[k+1] && low[k] < lowest(low, pivotStrength)[k-pivotStrength]  // evaluated at k >= pivotStrength; lastSwingLow = most recent k with isSwingLow(k)

complexity.reason: swing-pivot detection with a confirmation lag; the design decision is pivot strength and how many pivots to retain

notes: Brooks never states a pivot strength; he reads swings visually. 2 bars each side is a conservative default for 5-minute charts.

candidates.name: AlwaysInLong
candidates.quote: It is when the market becomes clearly always-in long in the eyes of most traders if the trend is a new bull trend, or always-in short in the case of a new bear trend.
candidates.description: Shared primitive / context filter: the market is 'always-in long', meaning a trader forced to hold a position would hold a long. Brooks ties the flip to a strong breakout spike (see TP3-04). A design decision is needed: candidate proxies are (a) the last spike of N consecutive trend bars was bullish, (b) close above the EMA for the majority of the last M bars, (c) trending swings (TP3-08).
candidates.pseudocode: alwaysInLong = lastSpikeDirection == up  // proxy: the most recent run of spikeBars consecutive trend bars (TP3-04) closed up, and no opposite spike has since occurred

complexity.reason: 'always-in' is a discretionary read; a proxy must be chosen before it can be coded

notes: Gates most with-trend candidates in Chapters 18 to 20. Book 2 gives more detail; the dedup pass should merge all AlwaysIn definitions.

candidates.name: BullSpike
candidates.quote: if there is a strong bull breakout, or a trend from the open bull, where there is a bull spike made of four consecutive large bull trend bars with small tails, and then the fifth bar falls below the low of the prior bar, this is a pullback.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a bull spike is spikeBars consecutive bull trend bars with small tails and little overlap. Used as the 'strong trend / always-in flip' trigger and as the context for the High 1 buy.
candidates.pseudocode: for i in 0..spikeBars-1: BullTrendBar(i) && SmallTails(i) && LittleOverlap(i)  // all true
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (structure primitive; Brooks enters at the market or above the prior bar during a spike)

complexity.reason: a fixed-length window loop over per-bar tests

notes: Brooks says a spike 'can be as brief as a single bar'; spikeBars should be optimized from 1 upward.

candidates.name: LittleOverlap
candidates.quote: very little overlap between adjacent bars, and small tails. This is the spike phase of a trend
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar overlaps the prior bar by no more than a fraction of its own range (bull form: the low is at or near the prior bar's close/high).

complexity.reason: two-bar arithmetic

notes: Overlap of ranges is direction-agnostic, hence sides=same; Chapter 19 gives the sharper bull form low[0] >= close[1] - tick.

candidates.name: SmallTails
candidates.quote: a series of trend bars with large bodies, very little overlap between adjacent bars, and small tails
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the combined upper and lower tails of the bar are at most a fraction of the bar's range.
candidates.pseudocode: ((high[0] - max(open[0], close[0])) + (min(open[0], close[0]) - low[0])) <= tailFraction * (high[0] - low[0])

complexity.reason: single-bar arithmetic

candidates.name: HigherLowFormingBeforeBuy
candidates.quote: a trader usually should not be looking to buy unless the market is at least forming a higher low and should not be looking to short unless the market is at least forming a lower high.
candidates.description: Context filter: allow longs only when the most recent swing low is above the swing low before it (a higher low has formed).

complexity.reason: needs two retained swing-low pivots

notes: A cheap proxy: lowest(low, n)[0] > lowest(low, n)[n] with n as the leg length.

candidates.name: TrendingSwings
candidates.quote: then have trending swings (e.g., a series of higher highs and lows in a bull trend). Absent either of these, there is no trend.
candidates.description: Context filter: bull trend structure = the last swing high is above the prior swing high AND the last swing low is above the prior swing low. Brooks calls the mirror 'the definition of a bear trend' (p315).

complexity.reason: needs four retained swing pivots

notes: Candidate proxy for TP3-03 AlwaysInLong.

candidates.name: PriorTrendLineBreakRequired
candidates.quote: All trends, no matter how small, must first break a trend line from the prior trend or a support or resistance line from a prior trading range, and then have trending swings
candidates.description: Context filter for reversal/new-trend longs: within the last N bars a close occurred above the bear trend line drawn through the two most recent swing highs of the prior down move. Page 317 repeats it as a hard requirement: a buy setup 'must include a prior break of the bear trend line'.
candidates.pseudocode: bearTL(k) = line through (priorSwingHighBar, priorSwingHigh) and (lastSwingHighBar, lastSwingHigh) projected to bar k; exists k in 0..lookbackBars-1 with close[k] > bearTL(k)

complexity.reason: trend-line projection from two swing pivots plus a lookback for the break

notes: Brooks also accepts a break of a horizontal support/resistance line from a prior trading range: proxy close > highest(high, rangeBars)[1].

candidates.name: FirstPullbackAfterTrendLineBreak
candidates.quote: The best risk/reward ratio occurs when you enter on the first pullback after a trend line break, before there is a clearly established trend.
candidates.description: Buy the first pullback that follows a break of the prior bear trend line: after the break (TP3-09 within N bars), the first bar with low below the prior bar's low is the pullback; enter when a later bar closes above that pullback bar's high.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the pullback (signal) bar high

complexity.reason: trend-line break detection plus a persistent pullback counter

candidates.name: WithTrendOnly
candidates.quote: Depending on how you define a trend and a reversal attempt, about 80 percent of attempts to reverse a trend will fail.
candidates.description: Context filter: take entries only in the direction of the established trend (long side allowed when always-in long). Blocks all countertrend entries.

complexity.reason: inherits the always-in definition problem

notes: Concrete proxies: close > EMA(close, 20) for k of the last n bars; TP3-08 TrendingSwings.

candidates.name: StrongTrendDayFollowThrough
candidates.quote: if today was a huge bull trend day, especially if it was a reversal or a breakout and a possible start of a big move, the day will usually close near its high and the next day will also usually have a close above its open.
candidates.description: On daily bars: yesterday was a huge bull trend bar (range at least rangeMultiple times the average range, closing in the top closeFraction of its range) -> buy today's open, expecting close above open. Intraday form: after such a day, take long entries only and hold to the close.
candidates.pseudocode: (high[1] - low[1]) >= rangeMultiple * avgRange(rangeLookback)[2] && close[1] > open[1] && (close[1] - low[1]) >= closeFraction * (high[1] - low[1])
candidates.book_order_type: market on the next day's open

complexity.reason: average range over a window plus fixed-offset comparisons

notes: Pair with an exit at the next bar's close (NumBars(1)) to test the 'close above open' claim directly.
Brooks adds 'this may continue for several days in a row'.

candidates.name: OpeningSelloffToHigherTimeframeEMA
candidates.quote: The opens often have sharp sell-offs that trap bulls out and bears in but usually find support at the 15 or 60 minute moving average or at some other support level
candidates.description: Day after a strong bull trend day: buy the early sell-off when a bar's low touches the higher-time-frame moving average (approximated on the trading chart by a longer EMA, e.g. 20-bar EMA of 60-minute bars = 240 bars of 5-minute) within the first N bars of the session.
candidates.pseudocode: priorDayStrongBull && barsSinceSessionOpen <= openWindowBars && low[0] <= EMA(close, htfEmaLength)[0] && close[0] > EMA(close, htfEmaLength)[0]
candidates.book_order_type: limit / stop above the reversal bar at the moving average

complexity.reason: EMA plus session-open bar counting plus the prior-day flag

notes: Brooks refers to the 15 or 60 minute chart's MA; a long EMA on the base chart is the single-series stand-in.

candidates.name: InsideBarIsPullback
candidates.quote: Any bar or series of bars that represents any pause or loss of momentum is a pullback, even if there is no actual backward movement. This includes a single inside bar
candidates.description: In a bull spike, a single inside bar counts as a pullback (a pause bar): buy when the bar after the inside bar closes above the inside bar's high.
candidates.pseudocode: high[1] <= high[2] && low[1] >= low[2] && BullSpikeEndedAt(2) && close[0] > high[1]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the inside bar high

complexity.reason: inside-bar test plus the spike window loop

candidates.name: PullbackBar
candidates.quote: Eventually, there will be a true pullback bar, with a low below the low of the prior bar.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a bull-trend pullback bar is a bar whose low is below the prior bar's low.

complexity.reason: two-bar comparison

candidates.name: High1InBullSpike
candidates.quote: Once there is, other bulls will place stop orders to buy above its high, because this bar is a high 1 buy setup in a strong bull spike and therefore a high probability buy setup.
candidates.description: After a bull spike of spikeBars consecutive bull trend bars, the first pullback bar (low below prior low) is the High 1 signal bar; buy when a bar within the next maxWaitBars closes above that signal bar's high.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the pullback bar high

complexity.reason: needs a persistent 'spike seen, pullback seen' state across bars

notes: Chapter 18 restates: 'buying a high 1 pullback in a strong bull spike, but not after a buy climax'.

candidates.name: ShallowPullbackLimitBuy
candidates.quote: They place limit orders at and below the low of the prior bar, hoping for a small dip, so that they can get long. Because of this, the first pullback usually only falls below the low of the prior bar by a few ticks.
candidates.description: During a bull spike, a bar dips below the prior bar's low by no more than dipTicks (a shallow pullback that a limit order at/below the prior low would have caught) -> buy at the next open.
candidates.pseudocode: BullSpikeEndedAt(1) && low[0] < low[1] && low[0] >= low[1] - dipTicks * tickSize && close[0] > low[1]
candidates.book_order_type: limit at or a few ticks below the prior bar low

complexity.reason: spike window loop plus tick arithmetic

notes: Limit fills cannot be reproduced exactly at bar close; this is the close-based approximation.

candidates.name: BuyAbovePriorBarHighInSpike
candidates.quote: They have many ways to enter, like buying at the market, buying a one- or two-tick pullback, buying above the prior bar on a stop, or buying on a breakout above a prior swing high.
candidates.description: In an always-in-long market, buy when the bar closes above the prior bar's high (the close-based form of a buy stop above the prior bar).
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the prior bar high

complexity.reason: two-bar comparison; the context filter is separate

candidates.name: BreakoutAbovePriorSwingHigh
candidates.quote: When the trend is strong, strong bulls will buy the breakout above the old high (they are 'pressing,' or adding to, their longs) and there will be a measured move up of some kind.
candidates.description: In a strong bull trend, buy when the bar closes above the most recent swing high. Cheap proxy: close above the highest high of the last N bars ending one bar ago.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > lastSwingHigh   // proxy: close[0] > highest(high, lookback)[1]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the prior swing high

complexity.reason: true form needs a swing-high pivot; the highest-high proxy is simple

notes: Brooks stresses this only works while the trend is strong; once two-sided, the same new high is profit taking or a short (TP3-24).

candidates.name: BuyCloseOfAnyTrendBarInStrongBull
candidates.quote: They also buy on the close of both any bull or bear trend bar. They see the bear trend bar as a brief opportunity to buy at a better price and the bull trend bar as a sign that the market is about to move up quickly.
candidates.description: In a strong bull trend (always-in long), buy at the close of any trend bar, bull or bear (bear form is direction-agnostic: any bar whose body is at least bodyFraction of its range).
candidates.book_order_type: market at the close of the bar

complexity.reason: single-bar arithmetic; context filter separate

notes: Split further if useful: buy close of bull trend bar vs buy close of bear trend bar (Chapter 18 lists them separately).

candidates.name: ExitSpikeOnFirstNonTrendBar
candidates.quote: Others will wait for the bar to close, and if the bar is not another strong bull trend bar, they will sell at the close of the bar, realizing that they might be selling too early
candidates.description: Exit (partial in the book) a long entered in a spike when the current bar closes and is not another bull trend bar.
candidates.book_order_type: market at the close of the bar

complexity.reason: single-bar test on the exit side

notes: Add a minimum ctx.BarsSinceEntry() >= 1 so the entry bar itself cannot trigger it.

candidates.name: FinalHourWithTrendEntry
candidates.quote: When the market is in a bull trend, look for buy setups in the final hour. Likewise, when the daily chart is in a bear trend, look for sell setups in the final hour
candidates.description: Intraday: when the daily-chart trend is up (proxy: today's session close so far above the session open, or prior daily closes rising), allow/take long entries only in the final hour of the session. Page 316 adds the bear form: 'a huge plunge in the final 30 minutes' on bear days.
candidates.pseudocode: time[0] >= finalHourStart && dailyTrendUp   // proxy for dailyTrendUp: close[0] > sessionOpen && sessionOpen > priorSessionClose
candidates.book_order_type: any with-trend setup in the final hour

complexity.reason: time-of-day gate plus a session-level trend read that persists across bars

notes: Exit at the session close (TimeOfDayExit) is the natural partner.

candidates.name: FailedNewHighExpectsTenBarCorrection
candidates.quote: If the market reverses down hard, assume that the strong bears dominated at the new high and that the market will likely trade down for at least a couple of legs and at least 10 bars.
candidates.description: Context filter / short setup: after a breakout above the prior swing high, if within failBars a bear trend bar closes back below the old high, block new longs for at least blockBars bars (Brooks: a 10-bar, two-legged correction). Mirrored: a failed new low blocks shorts.
candidates.pseudocode: barsSinceFailedBreakoutAboveSwingHigh < blockBars  // failed breakout = close[k] > lastSwingHigh followed within failBars by a bear trend bar with close < lastSwingHigh
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context; the bears sell at the close and below the low of the reversal bar)

complexity.reason: swing-high reference plus a multi-bar failure test and a persistent countdown

notes: Page 311 also gives the other two outcomes: enough follow-through for a scalp = new buying (stay long); sideways = profit taking (buy lower).

candidates.name: NewHighAfterTwoSidedRallyIsShort
candidates.quote: If a rally to test the high has several small pullbacks within the leg up, with lots of overlapping bars, several bear bodies, and big tails on the tops of the bars, and most of the bull trend bars are weak, then the market is becoming increasingly two-sided.
candidates.description: Countertrend setup (written as the mirrored short-to-long form): when the rally into a new high shows two-sided signs (bear bodies, overlap, upper tails, weak bull bars) and, per p314, a prior pullback closed well below the EMA, the breakout above the old high is faded. Long form: fade a breakout below the old low after a two-sided sell-off.
candidates.pseudocode: twoSidedSelloff = BearBodyCount(n) >= k && AvgTailFraction(n) >= t && AvgOverlap(n) >= o; twoSidedSelloff && close[1] < priorSwingLow && close[0] > low[1]
candidates.book_order_type: sell above the old high (limit/scale) or below the reversal bar

complexity.reason: swing reference plus several window statistics and a failed-breakout test

notes: Kept as a composite; the components below are the mechanizable pieces.

candidates.name: BearBodyCountInWindow
candidates.quote: more and larger bear trend bars form and bars start to get tails on the tops. These are signs of selling pressure
candidates.description: Two-sidedness sign: the number of bars closing below their open in the last windowBars is at least minBearBodies. As a long filter, require the count to be BELOW the threshold (rally still one-sided).

complexity.reason: counting loop over a window

candidates.name: AverageUpperTailFraction
candidates.quote: big tails on the tops of the bars, and most of the bull trend bars are weak
candidates.description: Two-sidedness sign: the average upper-tail fraction (high minus the higher of open/close, over range) across the last windowBars exceeds tailFraction. As a long filter, require it to be below the threshold.
candidates.pseudocode: average((high[i] - max(open[i], close[i])) / (high[i] - low[i]), windowBars) < maxTailFraction

complexity.reason: window average of a per-bar ratio

notes: Guard zero-range bars.

candidates.name: AverageBarOverlapFraction
candidates.quote: with lots of overlapping bars, several bear bodies
candidates.description: Two-sidedness sign: the average range overlap between consecutive bars over the last windowBars exceeds overlapFraction of the bar range. Long filter: require it below the threshold.
candidates.pseudocode: average((min(high[i], high[i+1]) - max(low[i], low[i+1])) / (high[i] - low[i]), windowBars) < maxOverlapFraction

complexity.reason: window average of a two-bar ratio

candidates.name: LargerBearBarsAppearing
candidates.quote: As the two-sided trading increases and the sell-offs have more bear trend bars and last for more bars, the strong bulls will want to buy only at the bottom of the developing trading range
candidates.description: Two-sidedness sign: the largest bear body in the last windowBars is at least bodyMultiple times the average bull body in the same window. Long filter: require the opposite.
candidates.pseudocode: maxBearBody = highest(max(open[i] - close[i], 0), windowBars); avgBullBody = average(max(close[i] - open[i], 0), windowBars); maxBearBody < bodyMultiple * avgBullBody

complexity.reason: two window statistics

candidates.name: FadeBreakoutOfFirstLegInPullback
candidates.quote: the minor bull trend will usually reverse back down into the direction of the major bear trend after breaking out above the first or second swing high in the pullback.
candidates.description: Long form: in a bull trend, a pullback (minor bear trend) makes two legs down; when the second leg breaks below the first leg's swing low, buy the failed breakout (close back above that swing low). Page 315: 'the market reverses up after the breakout to a new low... a sign that the sell-off is more likely just a big pullback'.
candidates.book_order_type: limit at/below the prior swing low of the pullback, or stop above the reversal bar

complexity.reason: needs the pullback's internal swing low and the major-trend context

notes: Chapter 18 restates this as 'a breakout below a prior swing low in this small bear trend will fail, and they will buy there with a limit order'.

candidates.name: TrendAgeBars
candidates.quote: A trend that has gone on for 30 or more bars will often have an unusually strong breakout, but it can be an exhaustive climax.
candidates.description: Shared primitive / filter: the bull trend is mature, i.e. it has lasted at least minTrendBars bars. Proxy: bars since the close last crossed above the EMA, or bars since the lowest low of a long window.
candidates.pseudocode: barsSince(close crossed above EMA(close, emaLength)) >= minTrendBars   // alt proxy: lowestBar(low, longWindow) >= minTrendBars

complexity.reason: EMA plus a bars-since counter

candidates.name: ExceptionallyLargeTrendBar
candidates.quote: all strong bulls and bears love to see a large bull trend bar or two, especially if it is exceptionally large, because they expect it to be a brief, unusually great opportunity.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar is a bull trend bar whose range is at least rangeMultiple times the average range of the prior rangeLookback bars (a possible buy climax bar).

complexity.reason: window average of range

candidates.name: ExitOnClimaxBarInMatureTrend
candidates.quote: The bulls take profits on their longs and the bears initiate new shorts. Both sell aggressively at the close of the bar, above its high, at the close of the next bar (especially if it is a weaker bar)
candidates.description: Exit a long at the close of an exceptionally large bull trend bar once the trend has lasted at least minTrendBars bars (the second or third consecutive buy climax is the strongest case). Variant: exit at the close of the following bar if it is weaker (not a bull trend bar).
candidates.book_order_type: market at the close of the climax bar, or on the close of the next weaker bar, or below the low of the prior bar

complexity.reason: inherits the trend-age counter

notes: Third variant: 'sell below the low of the prior bar' = exit when close[0] < low[1] within N bars after the climax bar.

candidates.name: ConsecutiveClimaxCount
candidates.quote: especially if the move is the second or third consecutive buy climax, they step aside.
candidates.description: Filter: the number of exceptionally large bull trend bars (buy climaxes) in the last windowBars, with no bear climax between, is at least climaxCount -> block new longs / expect a correction.

complexity.reason: counting loop over a window

notes: Brooks means consecutive climaxes separated by pushes, not adjacent bars; the count-in-window proxy is a simplification.

candidates.name: NoBuyUntilTenBarCorrectionAfterClimax
candidates.quote: the bulls will not consider buying again until at least a 10-bar, two-legged correction, and even then, only if the sell-off looks weak.
candidates.description: Filter: after a climax bar in a mature trend, block new longs until at least blockBars bars have passed (Brooks also wants two legs down, which is TP3-29's structure).

complexity.reason: bars-since counter keyed on a compound event

candidates.name: LargePullbacksMeanTradingRange
candidates.quote: Once a strong bull begins to have pullbacks that are relatively large, the pullbacks... behave more like trading ranges than bull flags... A new high is now a breakout attempt above a trading range, and the odds are that it will fail.
candidates.description: Filter: the depth of the most recent pullback (last swing high minus the subsequent lowest low) relative to the preceding leg's height is below maxPullbackFraction; otherwise breakout buys above the old high are blocked (expected to fail).

complexity.reason: leg height needs swing pivots

notes: Page 314: 'Every trading range is within either a bull trend or a bear trend'; while in the range the trend 'is no longer strong'.

candidates.name: PullbackClosedWellBelowEMA
candidates.quote: Once the bears are strong enough to push a pullback well below the bull trend line and the moving average, they are confident enough that the market will likely not go much higher and they will aggressively short above the old high.
candidates.description: Filter (tipping point): within the last lookbackBars a bar closed below the EMA by at least depthMultiple times the average range. When true, new highs are shorting opportunities, not buys; as a long filter require it false. Mirror (p315): a strong rally above the bear trend line and EMA flips the bear.

complexity.reason: EMA plus a window minimum of a derived series

notes: The 'well below the bull trend line' half is TP3-09's line projection; the EMA half is coded here.

candidates.name: MeasuredMoveTarget
candidates.quote: if enough bulls are pressing their long, the market will often go up for a measured move that is equal to the height of the wedge.
candidates.description: Profit target: exit the long when price reaches the breakout level plus the height of the pattern that preceded the breakout (wedge / trading range / prior leg). Proxy: height = highest(high, n) - lowest(low, n) over the range before the breakout bar.
candidates.pseudocode: target = breakoutLevel + heightMultiple * (rangeHigh - rangeLow); ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && high[0] >= target
candidates.book_order_type: limit at the measured move target

complexity.reason: needs the breakout level and the pattern height captured at entry time and held as state

notes: Brooks lists other profit-taking levels too: trend line, trend channel line, bottom of a trading range above.

candidates.name: TrendDayIdentifiedInFirstHour
candidates.quote: Although a trend can begin with any bar during the day, the majority of trend days begin within the first hour or so.
candidates.description: Intraday filter: after the first firstHourBars of the session, if the close is beyond the opening range by at least breakMultiple times the opening-range height, treat the day as a trend day and take only with-trend entries for the rest of the session.
candidates.pseudocode: barsSinceSessionOpen >= firstHourBars && close[0] > openingRangeHigh + breakMultiple * (openingRangeHigh - openingRangeLow)

complexity.reason: session-open detection and an opening-range state

notes: Brooks's own trend-day test is pattern recognition (Chapters 21 to 26); the opening-range break is a proxy.

candidates.name: RangeDayReversalTargetsMidpoint
candidates.quote: The odds are very high that the reversal will at least test the midpoint of the day's range.
candidates.description: Intraday profit target for a countertrend (fade) long taken near the day's low on a trading-range day: exit when the high reaches the midpoint of the session's range so far.

complexity.reason: session high/low state

notes: Brooks also warns not to take swing profits early on a range day because the opposite extreme is often taken out.

candidates.name: VolatilityExtremeNearBearEnd
candidates.quote: When the volatility reaches an extremely high level, the end of the bear trend is often near as traders give up responding to the whipsaws
candidates.description: Filter (daily): when the ATR is at its highest of the last extremeLookback bars (or above atrMultiple times its long average), block new shorts / look for long reversal setups. Long form allows longs only after the volatility extreme.

complexity.reason: ATR plus a window maximum

notes: Brooks pairs this with 'wait until there is a price action setup, and it must include a prior break of the bear trend line' (TP3-09).

candidates.name: AddOnFirstPullbackNotFade
candidates.quote: most traders who attempt this will lose, because most of the pullbacks do not fall far enough for a profit... they invariably end up missing the much more profitable long that forms a few minutes later.
candidates.description: Filter: within blockBars after a bull spike, block short entries (do not fade the spike for a scalp). Long form: within blockBars after a bear spike, block longs.

complexity.reason: bars-since counter keyed on the spike primitive

notes: Page 310: after a strong breakout 'the bears might not look to sell again for dozens of bars'.

rejected.quote: Your personal radar can tell you if the market is more likely in a trend... If you have a sense of uncertainty, the market is more likely in a trading range.
you might have to go all the way down to a 1 minute chart or a 100 tick or smaller chart to see them
rejected.reason: needs data below the bar (smaller time frame / tick chart)

rejected.quote: If a pullback occurs, they increase the size of their position... adjust their position size down to a level where their dollars at risk are the same
rejected.reason: position sizing / scaling in, not a bar condition; the engine trades fixed size

rejected.quote: In the absence of some rare, dramatic news event, traders don't suddenly switch from extremely bullish to extremely bearish.
Many longs bought puts to protect themselves in case of a severe reversal... most of their puts expire within a few months
rejected.reason: options positioning, data the engine cannot have

rejected.quote: In the fall of 2008, most hedge funds were down on the year and their sophisticated investors aggressively pulled their money out
So don't be eager to buy just because a stock is down a Fibonacci 38 percent, 50 percent, or even 62 percent.

chapter_summary: Part III's introduction defines trend, swing, leg and pullback, describes the spike-then-channel-then-trading-range life cycle of a trend, and explains how strong bulls and bears behave at new highs as a trend matures. It produced the shared primitives (BullTrendBar, SwingPivot, AlwaysInLong, BullSpike, PullbackBar, ExceptionallyLargeTrendBar, TrendAgeBars), the trend-structure filters (higher low, trending swings, prior trend-line break, with-trend only), the High 1 / shallow-pullback / buy-above-prior-bar spike entries, a family of two-sidedness statistics (bear-body count, upper-tail fraction, overlap, larger bear bars), climax exits and post-climax cooldowns, and a few intraday/daily ideas (strong-day follow-through, final-hour with-trend entry, opening sell-off to the higher-time-frame EMA, range-day midpoint target).
